jurisdiction_sources.note: 16 V.S.A. section 603(a) inventory: Mount Ascutney School District, a unified union district in the Windsor Southeast Supervisory Union (member towns: Windsor, West Windsor). Operates PK-12.

sources.note: Mount Ascutney SD: six directors, residency allocated Windsor 3 / West Windsor 3, elected by the voters of both towns (modified at-large "Hybrid Model"). Memberships minted 2026-10-26 (Walter's ruling) from the district's current official roster on the Windsor Southeast SU site -- the Mount Ascutney School Board page, supplied by the SU office (Laurie Brown) in reply to a records request and verified rendered 2026-10-26: Davis McGraw (Chair) 2028, Elizabeth Burrows (Vice Chair) 2027, Megan Reed (Clerk) 2029, Bill Yates (Treasurer) 2028, Elizabeth Frederick 2029, Amy McMullen 2027 -- all ELECTED with the term years as shown. The March 13, 2023 board agenda fetched earlier (Burrows, McMullen, McGraw, Roisman, Yates, Pedrick) is superseded (Roisman and Pedrick have since left the board); Bill Yates is independently corroborated as current by a 2026 official document (Act 170 committee minutes, October 14, 2026). Conflicts from news leads are disclosed on the McMullen and Reed memberships. Town of West Windsor Selectboard minutes, May 11, 2017 (official): the Articles of Agreement discussion for the merger records the board design -- "3 Windsor and 3 West Windsor members, but they would have to be voted on by both towns" (the "Hybrid Model") -- the 16 V.S.A. section 730(a)(2) modified at-large pattern. The district's 2021 Annual Report lists six "Mount Ascutney School Board Directors" (3 Windsor + 3 West Windsor by address). The adopted 2017 Articles of Agreement themselves were not located.

Windsor Southeast SU, Mount Ascutney School Board page (official; rendered page verified 2026-10-26): current roster with term years -- 2028 Davis McGraw (Chair), 2027 Elizabeth Burrows (Vice Chair), 2029 Megan Reed (Clerk), 2028 Bill Yates (Treasurer), 2029 Elizabeth Frederick, 2027 Amy McMullen. Supplied by Laurie Brown, WSESU, in reply to a CivicMirror records request, 2026-10-26.

Windsor Southeast SU, Mount Ascutney School Board page (official; rendered page verified 2026-10-26): lists Elizabeth Burrows, Vice Chair, term year 2027. IDENTITY: same person as the Windsor-1 state representative record -- her General Assembly biography (legislature.vermont.gov/people/single/2024/34722) states she lives in West Windsor and has served on the local school board, alternating as chair and member of the Mount Ascutney School District board each year since its inception; the district's 2021 Annual Report likewise lists Elizabeth Burrows of West Windsor/Brownsville as Vice Chair. Page supplied by Laurie Brown, WSESU, in reply to a CivicMirror records request, 2026-10-26.

Windsor Southeast SU, Mount Ascutney School Board page (official; rendered page verified 2026-10-26): lists Megan Reed, Clerk, term year 2029. Disclosure: a Vermont Standard news lead (April 2026; news, not an official source) named a Megan M. Reed among the interviewees for appointment to the McMullen seat; the district's current official roster lists her as a member with a 2029 year and she is minted as shown (elected). Page supplied by Laurie Brown, WSESU, in reply to a CivicMirror records request, 2026-10-26.

Windsor Southeast SU, Mount Ascutney School Board page (official; rendered page verified 2026-10-26): lists Bill Yates, Treasurer, term year 2028. Named William Yates in the district's 2021 Annual Report (West Windsor/Brownsville). Independently corroborated as a current member by the Act 170 Group 8 committee minutes, October 14, 2026 (WSESU Act 170 site). Page supplied by Laurie Brown, WSESU, in reply to a CivicMirror records request, 2026-10-26.

Windsor Southeast SU, Mount Ascutney School Board page (official; rendered page verified 2026-10-26): lists Amy McMullen as a member, term year 2027. Minted AS SHOWN per Walter's ruling, 2026-10-26, with this conflict disclosed: Vermont Standard news reports (March-April 2026; news, not an official source) say McMullen was re-elected to a three-year term on March 3, 2026 (def. Kaitlyn Gould; recount 255-222) and then resigned the board (and her Windsor town clerk and district clerk posts), with the board interviewing candidates (Gould, Megan M. Reed, May Paquin) for an appointment to her seat -- a March 2026 election would ordinarily run to 2029, not 2027, and a resignation would ordinarily end the membership. The district's current official roster nevertheless lists her as a sitting member with a 2027 year; the board's March-May 2026 minutes would settle it. IDENTITY: same person as the Town of Windsor justice of the peace record -- a Windsor resident (the district's 2021 Annual Report lists her as a Windsor member and its chair). Page supplied by Laurie Brown, WSESU, in reply to a CivicMirror records request, 2026-10-26.
